statements.label: thm:main
statements.text: There exists a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite.

statements.name: Finite-dimensional linear obstruction
statements.label: cor:nonlinear
statements.text: Let $G$ be the finitely generated torsion-free word-hyperbolic group constructed in Theorem \ref{thm:main}. For every commutative field $K$, every integer $n\geq 1$, and every homomorphism $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, \[ R_f(G)\subseteq\ker\rho. \] Consequently, one fixed nonidentity element of $G$ is killed by all these representations, simultaneously over all such fields and dimensions. In particular, $G$ is not linear over any commutative field.

statements.name: Triangle complex criterion
statements.label: thm:triangle-complex
statements.text: Let $K$ be a connected finite Euclidean triangle complex. Suppose there is $\eta>0$ such that every nonempty cyclically reduced closed edge walk in each vertex link has angular length at least $2\pi+\eta$. Then $\pi_1(K)$ is torsion-free and word-hyperbolic. Moreover, a nonempty closed edge path in $K$ is not nullhomotopic if every cyclic turn has link distance at least $\pi$. Here a turn compares the direction back along the arriving edge with the direction of the departing edge.

statements.name: Closed paths
statements.label: prop:closed-paths
statements.text: In $K$, or any compatible Euclidean simplicial subdivision of it, a nonempty closed edge path whose every cyclic turn has link distance at least $\pi$ is not nullhomotopic.

lean.scopeText:
The residual-finiteness question for hyperbolic groups asks whether every nonidentity element survives in some finite quotient. The formalized result gives a negative answer by constructing a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite.

Nonlinearity over every field is not a separate conclusion of the statement linked below.
